answers.answer:
No pea protein result is linked to growing origin, growing conditions, variety or harvest period.

Which pea protein measured lowest in each metal? Among independent results, the two Spanish concentrate brands had lead and cadmium not detected; of the Irish powders, the second was lower in cadmium and mercury, 15.4 µg/kg and below 0.2 µg/kg, against 40.6 and 4.3 µg/kg. In manufacturer data, the lowest cadmium was 1.0 µg/kg in a blend of isolate batches. Four independent products from two markets do not show that any source is reliably lower.

Can country of origin pick a lower-metal pea protein? Not yet: no published pea protein result names the growing region, and the blends with a stated production country were below an unprinted detection limit. Origin-linked lot results are the evidence that would answer it.

answers.answer:
The EU 0.10 mg/kg cadmium level for proteins from pulses applies to pea protein; the EU 1.0 mg/kg supplement level applies where it is sold as a food supplement. California's per-day levels for lead and cadmium apply to products sold there. China's bean rows are the nearest GB 2762 entries.

Does pea protein contain lead? Two independently tested retail powders contained 22.2 and 22.5 µg/kg lead, and two concentrate brands had none detected. Manufacturer tests quantified lead in 11 of 15 batches at 10 to 40 µg/kg.

Does pea protein contain cadmium? Yes: two retail powders had 40.6 and 15.4 µg/kg, and manufacturer batches 1.0 to 80 µg/kg. All are below the EU maximum level of 0.10 mg/kg (100 µg/kg) for proteins from pulses.

Is arsenic a concern in pea protein? It is unknown: inorganic arsenic has not been measured in any pea protein product. Total arsenic appears only in manufacturer tests, all below reporting limits of 10 to 100 µg/kg. Ask for inorganic arsenic on each lot.

Is pea protein lower in metals than whey protein? In the one study that measured both, both pea powders were above the whey median for lead, 8.6 µg/kg across 27 whey powders, and one pea powder had more cadmium than any whey powder. With two pea products this is a tentative comparison, not a rule.

Is pea protein lower in metals than rice protein? For lead, the one study that measured both found none detected in two pea protein brands and 175.40 ppb in one of two rice protein brands. Inorganic arsenic cannot be compared, because it has not been measured in pea protein; see [[ingredients/rice-protein]] for the rice evidence.

Are manufacturer test results independent? No: the GRAS notice results are tests run or commissioned by the manufacturers and submitted to FDA with a GRAS notice, not measurements by an independent laboratory or agency. The Index shows them as manufacturer tests and does not name the companies or products.

Which country grows the lowest-metal peas for protein? No published pea protein result names the growing region, so China, Vietnam, the USA and Canada cannot be compared. Origin-linked lot results would answer it.

Does organic pea protein have fewer metals? No pea-specific data exist; across a US market screen of protein powders of all types, organic products averaged three times the lead and twice the cadmium of non-organic ones. That screen did not separate pea protein.

Do flavored pea protein powders carry more metals? Across all protein powders in a US market screen, chocolate-flavored products averaged four times the lead and 110 times the cadmium of vanilla-flavored products. No study separates flavored pea protein.

How do I check a pea protein against California Prop 65? Multiply the lead concentration by the serving weight: 22.2 µg/kg × 0.030 kg = 0.666 µg per 30 g serving, against the 0.5 µg/day level. Warning requirements depend on more than this arithmetic.

What does "not detected" mean on a pea protein certificate? It means the result was below the laboratory's limit, not that the metal is absent. One survey reported pea blends as below detection without printing the limit, and another printed limits without a unit, so neither shows how low the metal was.

What should a pea protein supplier's test report include? The accredited laboratory's name and ISO/IEC 17025 status, the report number, the method, the quantification limit for each metal, inorganic arsenic as well as total arsenic, and the lot tested. The published evidence lacks inorganic arsenic and, in two studies, usable detection limits.

Does the EU limit metals in pea protein? Yes for cadmium: 0.10 mg/kg for proteins from pulses, and 1.0 mg/kg for food supplements in general. The Index has not yet transcribed the EU lead rows that may apply.

Does China set a limit for pea protein? GB 2762-2022 has no protein powder row; beans are limited to 0.2 mg/kg lead and 0.2 mg/kg cadmium. The 2025 edition replaced it from 2026-09-02, and its bean rows are not yet in the Index.

Does FDA Closer to Zero cover pea protein? No: its action levels cover foods for babies and young children.
